question: Who developed the theory of relativity?
facts: • Special relativity was published in 1905. • General relativity was presented in its final form in 1915.

question: Who joined the Muslim League in 1913?
facts: • Jinnah had earlier worked with the Indian National Congress. • He later became the leading figure of the Pakistan Movement.

question: Where is the Asian Development Bank headquartered?
facts: • ADB was established in 1966. • It focuses on development in Asia and the Pacific.

question: What does the crescent and star on Pakistan’s flag represent?
answer: The crescent represents progress; the star represents light and knowledge.
facts: • Pakistan’s national flag was adopted on 11 August 1947. • Green represents the Muslim majority and the white stripe minorities, in the conventional explanation.

question: Which city is sometimes called the City of Gold in Pakistan?
answer: Multan is sometimes given in local quiz material, but “City of Gold” is not a well-standardized official nickname.
facts: • Multan is widely known as the City of Saints. • It is famous for shrines, mangoes and blue pottery.

question: Which prophet is called Safiullah?
answer: Adam (AS) is commonly given the title Safiullah.
facts: • Safiullah is often glossed as “the chosen/pure one of Allah.” • Title conventions can vary among traditional sources.

question: What is the world’s largest tropical rainforest?
facts: • It spans several South American countries, especially Brazil. • A rainforest is not the same as a single national forest.

question: What is Pakistan’s national bird?
facts: • The chukar is a partridge species. • Pakistan’s national animal is the markhor.

question: Where is the Economic Cooperation Organization (ECO) headquartered?
facts: • ECO succeeded the Regional Cooperation for Development in 1985. • Its members include countries from West, Central and South Asia.

question: When were Pakistan's first general elections held on the basis of adult franchise?
facts: • These were Pakistan's first direct general elections. • The Awami League won a majority of the National Assembly seats, largely in East Pakistan.

question: Since when has Pakistan observed Defence Day on 6 September?
answer: The annual observance began in 1966, marking the first anniversary of the 1965 war.
facts: • Defence Day commemorates the defence of Pakistan during the Indo-Pakistani War of 1965. • It is observed every year on 6 September.

question: If yesterday was Friday, what day will it be the day after tomorrow?
facts: • Yesterday Friday means today is Saturday. • Tomorrow is Sunday, so the day after tomorrow is Monday.

question: When was the China-Pakistan boundary agreement signed?
facts: • The agreement delimited the boundary in the northern area between China and Pakistan. • The Karakoram Highway later improved road connectivity between the two countries.

question: What is the longest river in Asia?
facts: • It is about 6,300 km long, depending on measurement. • The Yangtze flows into the East China Sea near Shanghai.

question: What is 90% of 90?
facts: • 10% of 90 is 9; 90% is 9 × 9 = 81. • Percentage means “per hundred”.

question: When was the Conquest of Makkah?
facts: • It took place in Ramadan. • The conquest followed the breakdown of the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah.

question: What does “Badr” refer to, and what does the word mean?
answer: Badr is a settlement in present-day Saudi Arabia and the site of the Battle of Badr; the Arabic word is commonly glossed as “full moon”.
facts: • The battle took place in 2 AH (624 CE). • Badr lies southwest of Madinah.

question: Which city is often described as one of Pakistan's oldest continuously inhabited cities?
answer: Multan is often described this way, but the claim to be the single oldest depends on the definition and evidence used.
facts: • Multan is known as the “City of Saints” because of its many Sufi shrines. • The Indus Valley Civilization sites, such as Mohenjo-daro, are much older archaeological settlements but were not continuously inhabited cities in the modern sense.

question: How many idols were reportedly kept in the Kaaba before the Conquest of Makkah?
facts: • The idols were removed after the Conquest of Makkah in 8 AH. • The Kaaba is in Masjid al-Haram in Makkah.

question: What is the capital of Mongolia?
facts: • Mongolia is a landlocked country between Russia and China. • The name is also transliterated as Ulan Bator.

question: Which international organization did Pakistan join as a full member in 2017?
facts: • Pakistan became a full member in June 2017 at the Astana summit. • Pakistan had held SCO observer status from 2005.

question: Which prophet is mentioned most often by name in the Quran?
answer: Prophet Musa (Moses), peace be upon him; a commonly cited count is 136 mentions.
facts: • Counts can vary with counting method and name forms. • His story appears across many Surahs, including Al-Baqarah, Al-A'raf and Ta-Ha.

question: What is Earth's circumference?
facts: • The meridional/polar circumference is about 40,008 km. • Earth is an oblate spheroid, so its circumference varies by direction.

question: What minerals does the Saindak project produce?
answer: Copper and gold, with silver also recovered.
facts: • The project is in Chagai District, Balochistan. • Saindak is a copper-gold mine and processing project.

question: How many Muslims were martyred at the Battle of Uhud?
answer: About 70 Muslims were martyred; 85 is not the standard figure.
facts: • The battle occurred in 3 AH (625 CE). • Hamza ibn Abdul Muttalib (RA) was among those martyred.

question: What does IMF stand for?
facts: • The IMF was established in 1944 at the Bretton Woods Conference and began operations in 1945. • Its headquarters are in Washington, D.C.

question: What is the literal meaning of Islam?
answer: Submission or surrender to Allah; in Islamic usage, willing submission to God.
facts: • The word is related to the Arabic root s-l-m, associated with peace and submission. • A Muslim is one who submits to Allah.

question: They are three brothers. Ali is ___ of the three.
facts: • For three or more people/things, the superlative form is commonly used. • “Cleverer” is comparative; “cleverest” is superlative.

question: On which river is Diamer-Bhasha Dam being built?
facts: • The project is in the Gilgit-Baltistan/Khyber Pakhtunkhwa region. • Its aims include water storage, irrigation support and hydropower generation.

question: On which river is Mangla Dam built?
facts: • Mangla Dam is near Mirpur in Azad Jammu and Kashmir. • It was completed in 1967 and is used for water storage, irrigation and hydropower.

question: A train travels at 120 miles per hour. How far does it travel in 12 minutes?
facts: • 12 minutes = 0.2 hour. • Distance = speed × time = 120 × 0.2 = 24 miles.
